propositions: Repository-wide documentation and comments require audit against explicit standards covering punctuation, diction, formal voice, paragraph structure, filler elimination, and audience-appropriate tone.
Documentation must be classified by audience (client-facing external, internal architecture, or developer comments) and owned by one explicit shard to prevent duplication and ensure maintenance.
Automated prose validation creates false-positive risk and must be limited to deterministic rotted references, paragraph-local format parsing, and adjudication before enforcement.
Generated artifacts need explicit ownership through generator-local descriptor protocol and aggregate list rather than central per-artifact registry.
Exploration, challenge, and filtering phases must separate oversight responsibilities so each surface family receives dedicated review before adjudication.
